title: Trigeminal nerve: CN V anatomy
description: Map facial sensation and masticatory motor fibers without confusing trigeminal CN V with facial CN VII.

questions.question: What are the three branches of the trigeminal nerve?
questions.answer: Ophthalmic V1, maxillary V2 and mandibular V3 supply different facial territories. V3 also carries motor fibers to muscles of mastication.

questions.question: Which nerve supplies sensation to the cornea?
questions.answer: The ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve, especially through the nasociliary pathway, carries most corneal sensation.

questions.question: What is the trigeminal sensory root?
questions.answer: Large sensory root emerges from lateral pons into trigeminal cistern. Function: Conveys facial somatic sensation centrally.

questions.question: Where is the ophthalmic V1 located?
questions.answer: Passes superior orbital fissure into orbit; gives frontal, lacrimal and nasociliary branches. Function: Sensation from forehead, upper lid and cornea.

questions.question: What is the function of the nasociliary nerve?
questions.answer: Function: Carries corneal sensation through long ciliary nerves. Orbital V1 branch giving long ciliary, ethmoidal and infratrochlear fibers.
